verses.text: “Run up and down Jerusalem’s streets. Look around and check the open squares. If you can find even one person who does what’s right and goes after the truth, I’ll forgive this city.
They say, ‘As surely as the LORD lives,’ but their oaths are straight-up lies.”

LORD, aren’t your eyes looking for truth? You struck them, and it didn’t faze them. You brought them to ruin, and they still wouldn’t take correction. They set their faces harder than rock and refused to come back.
Then I thought, “These are the poor. They don’t know any better, because they don’t know how the LORD wants them to live or what their God’s law says.
I’ll go talk to the people in charge. They know the LORD’s way and their God’s law.” But they’d all broken the yoke and snapped their bonds together.

So a lion from the forest will kill them, a wolf at dusk will destroy them, and a leopard will lie in wait outside their cities. Whoever goes out will get torn apart. They’ve done wrong over and over and wandered further away.

“How am I supposed to forgive you? Your children walked out on me and swore by things that aren’t gods at all. I fed them until they were full, and they went and cheated. They showed up in crowds at prostitutes’ houses.
They were like well-fed horses roaming loose, each one neighing after his neighbor’s wife.
Should I let them get away with all that?” says the LORD. “Shouldn’t I take vengeance on a nation that acts like this?
“Climb her walls and tear things down, but leave some standing. Strip off her branches. They don’t belong to the LORD.
The families of Israel and Judah have both betrayed me badly,” says the LORD.
They’ve denied the LORD and said, “It’s not him. Nothing bad is coming for us. We won’t see war or go hungry.
The prophets are just wind. They don’t have his word in them. Let it happen to them instead.”
So the LORD, the God of Armies, says, “Because you all talk like this, watch what happens. I’ll make my words in your mouth fire, and these people will be the wood it burns up.

Listen, family of Israel. I’m bringing a nation from far away to come against you,” says the LORD. “They’re a strong nation that’s been around a long time. You don’t know their language, and you won’t understand a word they say.
Their arrow case is an open grave. Every one of them is a mighty warrior.

They’ll gobble up your harvest and the bread your sons and daughters should’ve eaten. They’ll eat your flocks and herds and strip your vines and fig trees. Those fortified cities you’re counting on? They’ll take them down with the sword.
“Even in those days,” says the LORD, “I’ll stop short of wiping you out completely.
When you ask, ‘Why did the LORD our God do all this to us?’ tell them, ‘You left me and served foreign gods in your own land. Now you’ll serve strangers in a land that isn’t yours.’
“Spread this through Jacob’s family and announce it in Judah. Say,
‘Listen up, you foolish people who don’t get it. You’ve got eyes and still don’t see, ears and still don’t hear.

Aren’t you afraid of me?’ says the LORD. ‘Won’t you tremble in front of me? I put sand there as a boundary for the sea and gave it a rule that lasts forever. Its waves can thrash all they like, but they won’t win. They can roar, but they can’t cross it.’
“But these people have stubborn, rebellious hearts. They’ve turned against me and walked off.
They never think, ‘Let’s fear the LORD our God. He gives us the early rain and the late rain when they’re due, and he keeps the set weeks of harvest for us.’
“Your wrongdoing pushed those things away. Your sins kept good things from reaching you.
There are wicked men among my people. They lie low like bird catchers. They set their traps, and it’s people they catch.
Their houses are packed with lies the way a cage is packed with birds. That’s how they got powerful and rich.
They’ve gotten fat and shiny, and they’re experts at doing wrong. They won’t take up the case of children without fathers so those children can thrive, and they won’t defend the rights of the needy.
“Should I let all that go unpunished?” says the LORD. “Shouldn’t I take vengeance on a nation that acts like this?
“Something shocking and horrible has happened in the land.
The prophets tell lies, the priests rule on their own authority, and my people love it like that. What are you going to do when it all comes to an end?”
